mainKeyword: all in one printers for home use
guideTitle: Best All-in-One Printers for Home Use (2026)
metaDescription: Six home all-in-one printers compared by ink system, paper tray, feeder and fax, so the machine matches how many pages your household really prints.
expertTake: The Canon MegaTank G3270 is the best home all-in-one for people who print steadily, because the ink supply in the box lasts about two years for a typical household. The HP DeskJet 2955 is the lowest-commitment machine for a student or an occasional printer. Anyone who prints under a hundred pages a year should read the section on idle clogging before choosing any inkjet.
introParagraphs: A home all-in-one has to do four jobs without fuss: print documents, copy a form, scan a page and put up with sitting unused for weeks. The ink system and the paper path decide how well it manages that, far more than the headline resolution.

Sort the choice by how much you print. Light users want a low purchase price and tolerance for idle time, regular users want cheap pages, and home-office users want a feeder, duplex and a bigger tray. Each of those points to a different machine.

products.name: Canon MegaTank G3270 refillable-tank all-in-one
specs: Up to 2 years ink in box

specList.label: Starter ink
specList.value: Up to 2 years in the box

products.description:
The G3270 puts ink in refillable tanks and ships with enough to last up to two years, which changes the economics of home printing. The listing quotes a yield of up to 6,000 black and white pages or 7,700 color pages from a single set of bottles, a figure that shows how little each page costs compared with a cartridge machine.

It is a compact desktop all-in-one that prints, copies and scans wirelessly. It has no document feeder, so it suits single pages, photos and school projects rather than stacks of paperwork. The tank system also removes the common failure of cartridges that expire before you use them, though regular printing is still the best defense against clogged heads.

Against the HP DeskJet 2955 it costs more up front and far less over a few years. Against the Brother INKvestment 4355, it uses a simpler bottle refill instead of a cartridge-based tank, with fewer functions. Fill each tank slowly, keep the bottle upright and wipe any drip from the port.
products.bestFor: Families that print every week and want to stop buying ink.
pros: Starter ink lasts up to two years
cons: Refilling can be messy if rushed

products.name: Brother INKvestment 4355 tank-style all-in-one with fax
specs: Up to 1 year ink in box

specList.label: Starter ink
specList.value: Up to 1 year in the box

products.description:
The Brother INKvestment 4355 uses an internal ink tank system that you top up through front-loading cartridges, which the listing says provides up to one year of ink in the box. It is a halfway design between a pure refill tank and a conventional cartridge printer, and it avoids the mess of pouring ink.

It prints, copies, scans and faxes, with fast speeds, duplex printing and a 20-page automatic document feeder, so it handles a small stack of paperwork where the Canon G3270 cannot. A 1.8 inch color display and a manual feed slot help with envelopes and card stock.

Compared with the HP OfficeJet Pro 8135 below, it offers a longer ink supply in the box and a lower running cost, but a smaller tray. Compared with the TR8620a, it uses an ink system aimed at long supply rather than photo quality. Keep spare cartridges because they are what refill the internal tank.
products.bestFor: Home offices that want long ink supply and duplex.
pros: Up to one year of ink in the box
cons: More complex than a basic model

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR8620a 4-in-1 with feeder and fax
products.description:
The TR8620a is the multi-purpose household machine, with print, copy, scan and fax in one body plus an automatic document feeder. The listing stresses both photo and document printing, which makes it the pick if family photos and school work share a printer.

It connects to Alexa and can send low-ink notifications and reorder supplies, and the listing says enrolling in the reorder service carries no subscription. That addresses the habit of running out at the worst moment, though you will still be buying cartridges, and cartridge cost per page is higher than on a tank model.

Against the Canon TS6520 it adds a feeder and fax and takes more desk space. Against the G3270 it costs more per page and offers better photo handling. Use it if the mix of photos and paperwork is the point, and expect to replace cartridges more often than on the tank machines.
products.bestFor: Households that print photos and paperwork on one machine.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 all-in-one with 1.42 in OLED display
products.description:
The TS6520 is a compact home all-in-one with a small OLED display and a two-cartridge ink system. The listing calls it an affordable, versatile machine for home users and hybrid workers, with crisp documents and photos from its cartridge pair.

It does not include a feeder or fax, so it is the simpler machine of the two Canon cartridge models here. That keeps it small and cheap, and setup from a smartphone or computer is straightforward. For a household that prints a few pages a week, it does the job without much to learn.

Compared with the TR8620a, it gives up the feeder and fax for a smaller body and lower cost. Compared with the HP DeskJet 2955, it offers a better display and a more photo-oriented cartridge set. Print something every couple of weeks to keep the nozzles open.
products.bestFor: Small households that print a few pages a week.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8135 all-in-one with fax, duplex and ADF
products.description:
The OfficeJet Pro 8135 is the busiest-office pick here: fast color printing, automatic two-sided output, an automatic document feeder and a 225-sheet input tray, plus fax. If someone in the house works from home and prints most days, the tray and duplex save real time.

The listing includes a three-month trial of Instant Ink, a delivery subscription, and the printer is part of HP's connected ecosystem. Read the program terms before you start, since subscription ink can change what you may use and what you pay if you stop the plan.

Compared with the Brother 4355, it has a larger tray but a shorter ink supply in the box. Compared with the G3270, it is much faster and better at documents but costs more per page. Choose it for daily work, and for light home use, one of the smaller machines is the better fit.
products.bestFor: Daily home-office printing with duplex and a large tray.
cons: Higher cost per page than tank models
Bigger and pricier than home models

products.name: HP DeskJet 2955 basic wireless all-in-one
products.description:
The DeskJet 2955 is the entry-level machine: color printing, copying, scanning, wireless and mobile printing and a 60-sheet input tray. The listing describes it as suited to basic needs such as to-do lists, letters and financial documents.

The small tray means more refills, and the lack of feeder, duplex and any tank system keeps cost and size down. That is the right trade for a student or someone who prints a few pages a month, because buying a larger machine that sits idle is how people end up with clogged heads and expired cartridges.

Compared with the TS6520, it is simpler and often cheaper. Compared with the G3270, it will cost more in ink over time. Treat it as a starter, and if your printing grows, graduate to a tank model rather than feeding this one cartridges at a high cost per page.
pros: Lowest purchase price in the guide
cons: Expensive per page for regular use

buyingCriteria.criterion: Match ink system to page count
buyingCriteria.explanation: The Canon G3270 ships with up to two years of ink and quotes yields of 6,000 black and 7,700 color pages per set, which suits steady printing. The DeskJet 2955 and TS6520 use cartridges that cost less to buy and more per page. Add up how many pages you print a year before choosing, because that decides which one is cheaper.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Consider a feeder and duplex together
buyingCriteria.explanation: The Brother 4355 and HP 8135 combine a feeder with automatic duplex, while the TR8620a has a feeder and manual duplex only. If you handle paperwork, those two features turn a chore into a button press. If you print photos and the odd letter, they are wasted size and cost.

A 60-sheet tray on the DeskJet 2955 means reloading often, and a 225-sheet tray on the HP 8135 means loading a ream every few weeks. For a student the small tray is fine. For a home office, a larger tray is a real convenience, since running out of paper mid-job is a common annoyance.

The HP 8135 listing includes a three-month Instant Ink trial. Subscription ink can be cheap for steady use but ties you to a plan and may limit third-party cartridges. The Canon TR8620a offers Alexa reorders with no subscription. Read the terms so you know what happens if you stop paying.

Inkjet heads dry out when unused, and the cleaning cycle that fixes it uses ink. A machine you will use weekly, like the G3270, avoids the problem. For rare use, buy a cheap model and print a color page every couple of weeks, or consider a laser, which is out of scope here.

The TR8620a, Brother 4355 and HP 8135 include fax. Most households never use it, but some offices and medical or legal forms still require it. If you do not need it, skip the extra cost and complexity, and use a phone scanning app for forms.

howWeEvaluated.description: We compared tank and cartridge machines using stated yields. The Canon G3270 quotes up to 6,000 black and 7,700 color pages per set of ink, which put it ahead of the cartridge models.

howWeEvaluated.title: Paper path and tray
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered tray size, duplex and feeder together. The HP 8135 and Brother 4355 offer the most complete paper handling, while the DeskJet 2955 offers the least.

howWeEvaluated.title: Functions for home use
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at whether fax or a feeder genuinely suits a household. The TR8620a bundles both and photos, and the TS6520 keeps to the basics.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ink programs and reordering
howWeEvaluated.description: We read the listings for subscription terms and reorder tools. The HP 8135 includes an Instant Ink trial and the Canon TR8620a offers Alexa reorders without a subscription.

howWeEvaluated.title: Behavior when idle
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how each ink system copes with weeks of non-use. Tank machines are used more, and cheap cartridge machines work if you print regularly.

cards.label: Cartridge
cards.text: The DeskJet 2955, TS6520 and TR8620a use cartridges. They are cheap to buy, easy to swap and fine for light use, but they cost more per page and can expire unused.

cards.label: Tank or tank-style
cards.text: The Canon G3270 and Brother 4355 carry a large ink supply in the box. They cost more up front and far less to run, which pays off for steady printing.

howToChoose.note: Heavy printers should choose tanks; occasional printers should choose cartridges.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Cheap pages, wireless printing from several devices and a tray that holds enough paper for homework weeks. Color matters for projects, and a scanner helps with worksheets.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Canon MegaTank G3270 prints a lot of pages cheaply, and the TS6520 handles light school use at lower cost. Both print wirelessly from phones and tablets.

cards.text: You print weekly or work from home. The Canon G3270 saves on ink and the HP 8135 or Brother 4355 save time with duplex and a feeder.

cards.text: You print rarely. The HP DeskJet 2955 or Canon TS6520 cost little, and a cheap machine that sits idle costs less than an expensive one that does.

maintenance.why: Regular output keeps nozzles open. A page with color blocks exercises every channel.
Running a tank dry can introduce air into the lines. Refill before the low mark.
Smudges show on copies. A dry microfiber cloth is enough.
Self-maintenance runs when the printer is on, and a machine pulled from the wall can leave heads uncapped.
Dusty rollers cause misfeeds. A damp lint-free cloth restores grip.

faq.q: Is a tank printer worth the extra cost?
faq.a: It is if you print weekly. The Canon G3270 ships with up to two years of ink, and bottles cost little per page. For a few pages a month the cheaper cartridge machine is fine.

faq.q: Do I need a document feeder?
faq.a: Only if you scan or copy multi-page documents often. A flatbed handles single pages and photos, and your phone can scan a few forms.

faq.q: What is the catch with subscription ink?
faq.a: It can be cheap for steady use, but it ties you to a plan and may restrict other ink. The HP 8135 includes a trial, so read the terms before you continue.

faq.q: Why does my printer waste ink on cleaning?
faq.a: Cleaning cycles clear dried nozzles by pushing ink through them. They run more often when a printer sits unused. Printing regularly reduces them.

faq.q: Can I print from my phone?
faq.a: Yes. Every machine here prints wirelessly from phones and tablets, and most are set up through the maker's app or the phone's built-in printing system.

faq.q: How long should a home printer last?
faq.a: Many last five years or more with regular use. Clogged heads and worn feed rollers are the usual failures, and both are easier to avoid with steady use and clean paper.
